abstract: Metabolic alterations in the posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) emerge early in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but their molecular and cellular basis remains unclear. We hypothesized that impaired glial energy metabolism, particularly mitochondrial oxidative metabolism in astrocytes, underlies the metabolic vulnerability of the PCC in AD. To test this hypothesis, we integrated human PCC proteomics and transcriptomics with magnetic resonance spectroscopy in AppNL-G-F knock-in (APP-KI) mice. Human proteomic and transcriptomic analyses converged on reduced mitochondrial oxidative-metabolism signatures associated with AD pathology and cognition. APP-KI hippocampus showed proteomic and 1H-MRS alterations resembling those in the human AD PCC. Spatial transcriptomics identified widespread metabolic transcriptional changes and reduced mitochondrial pathway signatures in glia-enriched hippocampal clusters. Hyperpolarized [1-13C]pyruvate spectroscopy showed reduced bicarbonate labelling in APP-KI mice, consistent with impaired oxidative pyruvate metabolism. These findings reveal convergent mitochondrial alterations in human AD and APP-KI mice, implicating glial cells, particularly astrocytes, in the associated dysfunction.
